description: Custom Calculator Builder Tools - Build and manage TIER 2E custom calculators with formula-based execution (6 interactive tools)

tools.name: calculator_builder_start
tools.short_description: START HERE! Initialize new custom calculator with name, description, and category
tools.description: Initialize a new custom calculator in the database with draft status. This is STEP 1 of the calculator building process. Creates calculator record and returns calculator_id for subsequent operations. BEFORE using: Call custom_calculator_get_schema_guide() to understand system architecture and see example calculators. After creating: Use calculator_builder_add_parameter() to add input fields, calculator_builder_set_formula() to add calculation steps, calculator_builder_add_component() to add reusable logic, calculator_builder_test() to test with sample inputs, calculator_builder_save() to activate when ready. Returns: calculator_id (UUID to use in all subsequent builder calls), suggested_parameters (top 10 most-used parameters from library for quick reference), name, category, is_active (false=draft status), created_at timestamp. Optional: Can clone from existing calculator by providing based_on_calculator parameter to copy structure as starting point.

name.description: REQUIRED: Unique calculator name for internal references. Use PascalCase without spaces (e.g., 'CustomVinylRushJob', 'LargeBannerSpecialty'). Must be unique across all custom calculators. Max 255 characters. Will be used in API calls and database queries.

description.description: REQUIRED: Detailed explanation of what this calculator is for and when to use it. Be specific about: What products/services it covers, what makes it different from standard calculators, typical use cases, any special pricing rules. This helps users discover and understand the calculator. Max 5000 characters.

short_description.description: REQUIRED: Brief one-line summary for listings and search results. 50-500 characters. Should quickly convey what calculator does. Example: 'Rush vinyl stickers with 24-hour turnaround premium pricing'

category.description: REQUIRED: Grouping category for organization. Suggested categories: 'custom_quote' (non-standard jobs), 'specialty_substrate' (unusual materials), 'rush_job' (expedited turnaround), 'large_format' (oversized printing), 'complex_finishing' (multi-step finishing), 'seasonal_pricing' (holiday/event pricing), 'customer_specific' (client agreements), 'what_if_scenario' (testing). Can create new categories as needed.

tags.description: Optional: Array of searchable tags for discovery. Use specific keywords: materials (vinyl, canvas, corflute), finishes (laminate, die-cut, grommet), urgency (rush, same-day, overnight), size (large-format, small-run, bulk), etc. Example: ['vinyl', 'rush', 'outdoor', 'laminated']. Improves searchability.

based_on_calculator.description: Optional: Name of existing calculator to clone as starting point. If provided, copies json_definition structure from that calculator. Useful for creating variants. Example: Clone 'VinylStickerStandard' and modify for rush pricing. Can clone from both custom and hardcoded calculators.

returns.description: Success status, calculator_id (UUID for subsequent builder calls), name, category, is_active (false=draft), created_at, and suggested_parameters (top 10 most-used pricing parameters for quick reference). On error: success=False with error message and error_type

tools.name: calculator_builder_add_parameter
tools.short_description: Add input parameter (user input field) to calculator definition
tools.description: Add input parameter to calculator's json_definition. Input parameters are user-facing fields that customers fill in (width, height, quantity, material choice, etc.). This is STEP 2 of calculator building (after calculator_builder_start). Each parameter becomes a variable available in formulas. Supports 4 parameter types: 'integer' (whole numbers like quantity), 'number' (decimals like dimensions), 'select' (dropdown choices like material type), 'boolean' (yes/no like lamination). Can reference pricing parameter library using source field (e.g., source='calculator_pricing_parameters:labor_rate_trade' to use global labor rate). Parameters are stored in json_definition.inputs array and also tracked in custom_calculator_parameters table for impact analysis. Returns: success status, parameter added, current parameter count, and updated input parameters list. Call this multiple times to add all required inputs before adding calculation steps.

calculator_id.description: REQUIRED: Calculator UUID from calculator_builder_start() response. Must be valid UUID for draft or active calculator.

parameter_name.description: REQUIRED: Variable name to use in formulas (e.g., 'width_mm', 'quantity', 'material_type'). Use snake_case, no spaces. Must be valid Python identifier. Will be referenced in calculation_steps formulas and component inputs. Max 255 characters.

parameter_type.description: REQUIRED: Data type for input. 'integer' for whole numbers (quantity, sheets), 'number' for decimals (width_mm, price), 'select' for dropdown choices (material type, finish), 'boolean' for yes/no (lamination, rush). Affects validation and UI rendering.

label.description: REQUIRED: User-facing label for input field. Use proper capitalization and spacing (e.g., 'Width (mm)', 'Quantity', 'Material Type'). Shows in UI above input field. Max 255 characters.

description.description: Optional: Help text explaining what this input is and how to use it. Shows as tooltip or below input field. Example: 'Width of sticker in millimeters. Measure from left edge to right edge.' Be specific and helpful.

required.description: REQUIRED: Whether this input is mandatory (true) or optional (false). Required inputs must be provided before calculator can execute. Most inputs should be required except for optional add-ons. Default: true

default.description: Optional: Default value if not provided. Must match parameter_type (integer for integer type, etc.). Use for common values to reduce user input. Example: default=1 for quantity, default=false for rush delivery. Null if no default.

options.description: REQUIRED for parameter_type='select': Array of choice objects with {value, label}. Example: [{value: 'vinyl', label: 'Vinyl'}, {value: 'canvas', label: 'Canvas'}]. Value is used in formulas, label shown to user. Must have at least 2 options.

source.description: Optional: Reference to pricing parameter library. Format: 'calculator_pricing_parameters:parameter_name'. Example: 'calculator_pricing_parameters:labor_rate_trade' to use global labor rate. When provided, parameter value is resolved from database instead of user input. Tracks in custom_calculator_parameters table for impact analysis.

validation.description: Optional: Validation rules object. For number/integer types can include {min: 1, max: 10000} for range. For select can include custom validation. Example: {min: 100, max: 5000} for width_mm to enforce size limits. Prevents invalid inputs.

returns.description: Success status, parameter_name added, parameter_type, parameter_count (total inputs now), source_table (where parameter comes from), and current_inputs (full inputs array). On error: success=False with error message

tools.name: calculator_builder_set_formula
tools.short_description: Add formula calculation step using asteval safe evaluation
tools.description: Add formula-based calculation step to calculator's calculation_steps array. Formulas use asteval safe Python expression evaluator - supports arithmetic, comparisons, logic, and built-in functions. This is STEP 3 of calculator building (after adding parameters). Each formula step creates a new variable that can be referenced by subsequent steps. Formula syntax: Can reference input parameters, previous step variables, pricing constants (param:name). Allowed operations: +, -, *, /, **, %, <, >, <=, >=, ==, !=, and, or, not. Allowed functions: min, max, abs, round. NOT allowed: imports, file I/O, system calls, lambda, exec. Steps execute sequentially - each step can only reference previous steps and inputs. Returns: success status, step number added, variable name created, formula string, current step count. Call multiple times to build complete calculation sequence. Steps are auto-sorted by step_number.

calculator_id.description: REQUIRED: Calculator UUID from calculator_builder_start() response.

step_number.description: REQUIRED: Sequence number for this step (1, 2, 3, ...). Steps execute in order. Each step can reference previous steps only. If step_number exists, it updates that step, otherwise inserts new step.

variable_name.description: REQUIRED: Variable name to store calculation result. Use snake_case (e.g., 'area_m2', 'unit_price', 'subtotal'). Must be valid Python identifier. Will be available to subsequent steps and in final result breakdown. Max 255 characters.

formula.description: REQUIRED: Mathematical expression to evaluate. Can reference: input parameters (width_mm, quantity), previous steps (area_m2), pricing constants (param:gst_rate). Supports: +, -, *, /, **, %, <, >, <=, >=, ==, !=, and, or, not, min(), max(), abs(), round(). Examples: '(width_mm * height_mm) / 1000000', 'base_cost * (1 + param:profit_margin)', 'max(calculated_price, param:minimum_order)'. NO imports, NO file operations, NO system calls.

description.description: Optional: Plain language explanation of what this step calculates. Example: 'Calculate area in square meters', 'Add profit margin to base cost'. Shows in calculation breakdown. Helps users understand pricing logic.

returns.description: Success status, step_number added, variable_name created, formula, step_count (total calculation steps), and current_steps (all calculation steps). On error: success=False with error message and formula syntax error details

tools.name: calculator_builder_add_component
tools.short_description: Add pre-built component step (tiered pricing, GST, discounts, labor, etc.)
tools.description: Add component-based calculation step using pre-built functions from common_components.py. Components are tested, optimized, reusable logic blocks for common calculations. This is ALTERNATIVE to calculator_builder_set_formula for complex logic. 11 available components: tiered_pricing_lookup (51-tier pricing tables), quantity_break_discount (volume pricing), calculate_profit_margin (markup), apply_complexity_multiplier (job complexity), calculate_gst (10% GST), calculate_double_gst_shopify (Shopify double GST), calculate_area_m2 (mm to m² conversion), calculate_labor_cost (with multipliers), calculate_material_waste (10% default), calculate_setup_cost (base + artworks), minimum_order_check ($45 minimum). Each component has specific input parameters. Component calls are tracked in custom_calculator_components table for analytics. Returns: success status, step number, component name, inputs mapping, component_count (how many components used). Call multiple times to add different components.

calculator_id.description: REQUIRED: Calculator UUID from calculator_builder_start() response.

step_number.description: REQUIRED: Sequence number for this step. Steps execute in order. If step exists, updates it, otherwise inserts new step.

variable_name.description: REQUIRED: Variable name to store component result. Use snake_case (e.g., 'base_price', 'gst_amount', 'labor_cost'). Available to subsequent steps.

component_name.description: REQUIRED: Name of component function to call. Must be one of 11 available components. See custom_calculator_get_schema_guide() component_library for full list with parameters and usage.

inputs.description: REQUIRED: Map of component parameter names to formula variables. Keys are component's expected parameters, values are variable names from inputs or previous steps. Example: {'lookup_value': 'area_m2', 'tier_table': 'pricing.vinyl_tiers'}. Each component requires specific inputs - check component_library in schema guide.

description.description: Optional: Explanation of what this component does in this context. Example: 'Lookup vinyl price from 51-tier pricing table based on area'. Shows in breakdown.

returns.description: Success status, step_number, variable_name, component_name, inputs mapping, step_count, component_count (total unique components), and current_steps. On error: success=False with error message

tools.name: calculator_builder_test
tools.short_description: Test calculator with sample inputs BEFORE saving/activating
tools.description: Execute calculator with sample inputs to verify logic works correctly. This is STEP 5 (before calculator_builder_save). Does NOT save to quote_history_archive - test mode only. Returns complete calculation breakdown showing: each step's result, final price (total_price and unit_price if quantity provided), execution time, and any errors. Use this repeatedly during development to test edge cases: minimum values, maximum values, typical orders, zero quantities, etc. Validates: all required parameters provided, formulas execute without errors, components receive correct inputs, parameter references resolve, calculation produces sensible result. Returns detailed step-by-step breakdown for debugging. If test fails, fix formulas/components and test again before saving.

calculator_id.description: REQUIRED: Calculator UUID from calculator_builder_start() response.

test_inputs.description: REQUIRED: Map of parameter names to test values. Keys must match parameter names defined in calculator. Values must match parameter types (integer, number, select value, boolean). Example: {'width_mm': 300, 'height_mm': 200, 'quantity': 50, 'material_type': 'vinyl_gloss', 'add_lamination': true}. Provide all required parameters.

returns.description: Success status, total_price (final calculated price), unit_price (if quantity provided), breakdown (step-by-step results with variable names and values), execution_time_ms (performance metric), inputs_provided, and any validation errors. On error: success=False with error details

tools.name: calculator_builder_save
tools.short_description: Save and ACTIVATE calculator for production use (or save as template)
tools.description: Save calculator and optionally activate for production use. This is FINAL STEP of calculator building. Auto-generates usage_instructions if not provided (based on inputs, steps, components). Sets is_active flag - when true calculator is ready for production quotes. Can save as template (is_template=true) for cloning starting point. Updates timestamp. After activation, calculator appears in custom_calculator_list() and can be executed via API. BEFORE saving: Test thoroughly with calculator_builder_test() to verify all logic works. Once activated, calculator can be used immediately. Can re-save to update definition - deactivate first if making breaking changes. Returns: success status, calculator_id, is_active status, is_template flag, usage_instructions (auto-generated or provided), and updated_at timestamp.

calculator_id.description: REQUIRED: Calculator UUID from calculator_builder_start() response.

usage_instructions.description: Optional: Detailed instructions on how to use this calculator. Explain what each input means, typical values, when to use this calculator vs others, any special considerations. If not provided, auto-generates based on inputs, parameters, and components. Max 5000 characters.

activate.description: REQUIRED: Set to true to activate calculator for production use (is_active=true), false to save as draft (is_active=false). Activated calculators appear in listings and can be executed. Draft calculators are hidden. Default: false (safe default - save as draft first).

as_template.description: Optional: Set to true to mark as template for cloning (is_template=true). Templates appear in template listings for use with based_on_calculator. Useful for creating reusable starting points. Default: false.

returns.description: Success status, calculator_id, name, is_active (production ready flag), is_template (clone source flag), usage_instructions (auto-generated or provided), parameter_count, step_count, component_count, updated_at. On error: success=False with error message

when_to_use: FINAL STEP after building and testing complete calculator
Want to activate calculator for production use
Need to save template for future cloning
Updating existing calculator with changes
Adding usage instructions for users
Ready to make calculator available via API
workflow: Step 1: Complete all calculator building (parameters, formulas, components)
Step 2: Test thoroughly with calculator_builder_test() - multiple scenarios
Step 3: Verify all tests pass and prices are correct
Step 4: Write clear usage_instructions (or let system auto-generate)
Step 5: Decide: activate for production or save as draft?
Step 6: Decide: save as template for cloning?
Step 7: Call calculator_builder_save() with activate flag
Step 8: If activated, calculator immediately available for use
Step 9: Verify with custom_calculator_list() or custom_calculator_get_detail()
Step 10: Test via API or UI with real customer scenarios
best_practices: ALWAYS test with calculator_builder_test() BEFORE activating
Write clear usage_instructions - helps users know when to use calculator
Start with activate=false (draft) until fully tested
Use activate=true only when ready for production
Save as template if calculator is good starting point for variants
Auto-generated usage_instructions are basic - add detail for better UX
Can re-save to update definition - careful with breaking changes to active calculators
Deactivate (activate=false) before making major changes to production calculator
Test in production environment after activation
Monitor usage_count and avg_calculation_time_ms after deployment
error_handling: Error: Calculator not found - Verify calculator_id is correct
Error: No calculation steps defined - Must add at least one formula or component step before saving
Error: No input parameters defined - Must add at least one input parameter before saving
Error: Invalid JSON definition - Calculator definition malformed, rebuild from scratch if needed

typical_use_cases: Activating fully tested calculator for production use
Saving draft calculator for future work
Creating template calculator for cloning
Updating existing calculator with improvements
Adding usage instructions for better discoverability

conversation_memory_hints.what_to_remember: Calculator activation status, whether saved as template, usage_instructions added
conversation_memory_hints.search_context: When user references saved calculator or production deployment
